page: Amazon Web Services c8id.24xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs and 48 physical cores based on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors running at 3.9 GHz. The processor configuration includes a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. Memory resources consist of 192.0 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 7 GHz, yielding a 2.0 GB memory-per-core ratio. Local storage is bundled with 5700 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes, and baseline network performance is rated at 40 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong multi-core capabilities, with a multi-core stress-ng score of 103770.34 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 22327.0. The instance excels in memory bandwidth, achieving a top-tier read-only small block cached speed of 7652.04 GB/sec and a strong uncached large block write speed of 157.78 GB/sec. CPU-bound operations are highly efficient, as evidenced by top-tier scores in Passmark CPU physics, encryption, and extended instructions. The hardware supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for tile and INT8 operations.

The server demonstrates high efficiency for database and web serving workloads, delivering 166.59 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and 159.75 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. For artificial intelligence workloads, the CPU-based LLM inference speeds reach 3858.09 tokens per second for prompt processing on a small 135M model and 39.94 tokens per second on a large 70B model, though text generation speeds remain moderate. Given the high compute density, fast DDR5 memory, and large local NVMe storage, this instance provides a resource-dense profile for compute-heavy applications, software compilation, and high-throughput database operations without requiring dedicated GPU hardware.
description: Amazon Web Services c8id.24xlarge is a compute-optimized server featuring 96 dedicated vCPUs and 48 physical cores powered by 3.9 GHz Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, it includes 192.0 GB of high-speed 7 GHz DDR5 memory and 5700 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The architecture supports advanced vector and matrix extensions, enabling top-tier performance in multi-core processing, software compilation, and cryptographic operations. Benchmark results show exceptional memory bandwidth and database performance, with Redis SET operations reaching 166.59 million operations per second. While lacking dedicated GPUs, its high-frequency cores and massive local storage make it highly efficient for compute-intensive workloads, static web serving, and large-scale database applications.
